answer_1.quote: We investigate ChatGPT's morphological capabilities using the wug test, an experimental paradigm in which a participant is asked to provide an inflected or derived form of a nonce word.
answer_1.outputs: inflected word forms (e.g., past tense verbs, nominal plurals, derived forms) for nonce strings

answer_2.quote: Results are evaluated using accuracy at k (acc@k), i.e., a model's response is regarded as correct if it is in line with any of the top k human responses.

answer_4.quote: Participants were asked to provide the past tense of the nonce word and given an example (wug → wugged) and the frame "They wug all the time. In fact, they __ just yesterday!". We report the accuracy of one annotator at a time against the judgments of all other annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Provide the correct inflected form (e.g., past tense, plural) of the given nonce word in a single word.
